claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children. Let me begin with a few questions.

**First, could you tell me the names and ages of the children you're claiming for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help assess your eligibility.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education at the moment. They finished school recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex currently in paid work or employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Does Alex live with you, or does he/she live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more important question to complete my assessment.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have a right to reside in the UK?** This is important for Child Benefit eligibility purposes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and have the right to be here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me now read the eligibility criteria to ensure I have the correct information before providing you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment.

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child **under 16**. However, there is an exception for children aged 16 or over - you can continue to claim if the child is under 20 and **stays in approved education or training**.

In Alex's case:
- Alex is 16 years old (so no longer in the under-16 category)
- Alex is not in approved education or training (you confirmed they finished school recently and aren't in education)
- Alex is not in paid work

Since Alex doesn't meet the criteria for the 16+ exception (being in approved education or training), Child Benefit eligibility has ended.

**However, there is one potential option:** You may be able to apply for a 20-week extension of Child Benefit if Alex registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to ask about this possibility.
